newsitem.title: UK: Fitch downgrades US West Inc snr debt shelf.
newsitem.headline: Fitch downgrades US West Inc snr debt shelf.

text.p: Fitch Investors Service said on Thursday it had downgraded the debt ratings of U.S. West Inc and its related entities.
It said it downgraded U.S. West Inc's 's senior debt shelf to BBB plus from A plus.
Fitch said in a statement the downgrade was based on the expected deterioration of the company's credit profile on completion of the Continental Cablevision, Inc. acquisition.
In addition, Fitch rates U.S. West Capital Funding's planned issuance of $400 million TOPRS BBB.
The TOPRS are subordinated and rank junior to all other U.S. West Capital Funding senior debt.
The ratings are downgraded as follows:
U.S. West -- debt exchangeable for common stock (DECS) to BBB plus from A plus.
U.S. West Capital Funding -- senior debt and MTNs to BBB plus from A plus.
Trust originated preferred securities (TOPRS) to BBB from A and commercial paper to F-2 from F-1.
U.S. West Communications, Inc. -- senior debt to A plus from AA minus and commercial paper to F-1 from F-1 plus.

The ratings were originally placed on FitchAlert on February 27 in response to U.S. WEst's announcement it would acquire Continental in a stock and cash transaction valued at approximately $11 billion.

Fitch said the high leverage of the acquired properties and significant capital expenditure requirements would make it more difficult for U.S. West's non-regulated businesses to fund their activities entirely with internally generated cash flow.

The statement said the ratings on U.S. West Communications continued to reflect the regulatory restrictions placed on its cash flow and took into consideration some level of implied support toward U.S. West Capital Funding.
"Fitch does not currently rate Continental's outstanding debt," the statement said.
"If U.S. West guarantees the debt of Continental, Fitch would most likely assign a rating consistent with those on U.S. West Capital Funding.
"If U.S. West does not guarantee the debt, it will be considered subordinated and would likely be rated lower than that of U.S. West Capital Funding," the statement added.
